title: Admission-gated native Blender 5.2 compiler integration
hypothesis: The B53-E1 admission module can guard the real restricted SceneSpec compiler entry with a relative evidence/output invocation, preserve total attempt receipts before Blender authorization, and still reproduce the frozen B01/B02 BuildPlan and canonical Blender structure identities across two fresh native builds per benchmark.

requirements: Commit and push this exact spec and protocol before creating any B54-E1 tool byte or output root.
Commit and push all three new exact tool bytes before creating the preflight root.
Run one zero-Blender preflight; commit and push accepted preflight evidence before creating attempt/formal roots.
The formal runner is single-use. Retain every partial output; any repair requires a new experiment ID.

forbidden: reuse or deletion of a pre-existing experiment output

admission.attemptLedger: Create the separately declared fresh attempt root and self-hashed attempt.json before calling admitFormalRun(). On accept write admission.json plus receipt.json before formal-root materialization; on reject write failure.json plus receipt.json with scientificVerdict null.
admission.authorizationBoundary: No Blender or restricted compiler process may start before accepted admission and its receipt are durable.

buildPlan.method: Call current compileBuildPlan() twice per benchmark in the formal runner, require canonical wrapper byte identity, require the frozen plan hash, and write one formal BuildPlan per benchmark only after admission.

requirements: Exact preregistration, B53 parent evidence, Node/Blender binary identities and all frozen tool hashes.
All spec/tool/input paths tracked-clean and tool-freeze commit pushed to origin/main.
Two in-memory compileBuildPlan calls per benchmark are canonical-byte exact and equal frozen plan hashes.
Relative preflight/formal path spellings pass a no-output admission-shaped component probe without creating attempt/formal roots.
Projected 512 MiB write leaves at least 100 GiB free.
Preflight, attempt and formal roots remain absent before accepted preflight creation.

formalOperationContract.processEvidenceBoundary: Direct child PIDs/exit codes are exact. Nested Blender compile PIDs are bound by budget reports. Existing receipt/verifier Blender --version probes are counted semantically from their frozen code paths but are not independently PID-attributed.

auditContract.independence: The auditor must not import the B54 preflight or runner. It may invoke the already-existing current CompileReceipt verifier as an external child, and must independently reopen canonical structure bytes, manifests, BuildPlans, admission records and .blend files.
auditContract.receiptVerification: B01-A/B and B02-A/B each pass the current verifier with exactly 19 checks.
auditContract.structureVerification: Parse every scene.structure.canonical.json, require deep equality with its adjacent manifest structure, require both manifest hash bindings, require A/B byte identity per benchmark and the two frozen hashes.
auditContract.blendVerification: Run blender/audit_compiled_artifact.py on all four .blend files and require embedded planHash, structureHash, manifest version and Blender build hash bindings.
auditContract.verdictValidation: Outcome-neutral: derive supported versus rejected from observed gates; a tool/process exception invalidates with scientificVerdict null.

decision.supportedWhen: All 18 gates pass, admission is durable before formal-root materialization, all four native compiles/receipts/blend audits pass, B01/B02 plan and structure identities remain frozen, and 24 or more semantic attacks are rejected.
decision.invalidated: Any frozen tool/process failure produces scientificVerdict null, preserves partial evidence and forbids same-ID repair or rerun.

nonClaims: This does not repair or rerun B52-D12.14-H2.
This does not claim deterministic .blend container bytes.
This does not render pixels or prove cinematic image quality.
B01/B02 are minimal compiler benchmarks, not full actor, cloth, hair, simulation or production-lighting coverage.
Local Git ancestry and SHA-256 receipts are not signatures or remote attestation.
Nested Blender identity-probe subprocess PIDs are not independently attributed by existing production tools.
A supported result does not silently modify existing frozen runners or replace the public production entry alias.
promotionBoundary: If supported, a later explicitly preregistered release step may expose the admission-gated wrapper as the preferred compiler entry. Existing runners remain immutable; any later compiler, receipt, admission or orchestration change must rerun the B01/B02 plan and structure regression gates.
